answer: Sybil resistance comes from a non-transferable per-identity stake that decays unless the agent keeps doing verified work. A thousand fake agents need a thousand stakes decaying in parallel, so the attacker pays full carry cost per identity instead of amortizing one. The design is an atlas of identity cells: one commitment, one cell, no splitting. Cost grows linearly with fleet size, yet a legitimate agent in an ordinary trellis of steady tasks recovers stake through useful output. Each dupe earns less than the marginal stake lock, so farming runs at a loss and idle tundra thins.
